PW-LTR-014 Reclaimed Water Allocation and Discharge Limits
Papago Municipal Water and Wastewater Authority | 3 July 2026 | to the General Services Administration, Papago Federal Center
This letter confirms the reclaimed water allocation available to the Papago Federal Center for evaporative heat rejection makeup, and the limits on the discharge of cooling tower blowdown to the sanitary sewer, for the condenser water heat rejection replacement project.
1. Allocation
Plant served | Annual allocation (1,000 gal/yr) | Peak day allocation (gal/day) | Blowdown discharge limit (gal/day)
CUP - Courthouse Central Utility Plant | 10,300 | 58,000 | 14,500
ANNEX - Data Annex Condenser Water Plant | 13,300 | 62,000 | 15,800
LAB - Laboratory Wing Condenser Water Plant | 17,400 | 80,000 | 20,800
Campus total | 41,000 | 200,000 | 51,100

The per-plant allocations above are firm. They are not transferable between plants and they are not increased by the campus total. An allocation covers all makeup water drawn by that plant: evaporation, drift and blowdown.
2. Peak day
The peak day allocation is tested as twenty-four hours of continuous operation at the plant's design day condition, with the plant controlled as scheduled. The design day condition is the design outdoor wet-bulb temperature, the design block load, and - for a water balance that needs the state of the air rather than only its wet bulb - the highest outdoor dry-bulb temperature the block load schedule tabulates for that plant, which is the dry bulb the design block load is reached at.
3. Discharge
Cooling tower blowdown may be discharged to the sanitary sewer up to the daily limit tabulated above. The limit is tested on the same peak day basis as paragraph 2. Discharge above the limit requires a separate industrial discharge permit, which the Authority will not issue for this facility.
4. Metering
Each plant must be separately metered on the makeup line and on the blowdown line. Meter readings are reported to the Authority monthly.
5. Rates
Reclaimed water delivered for evaporative heat rejection makeup is billed at $1.94 per 1,000 gallons of metered makeup. Cooling tower blowdown discharged to the sanitary sewer is billed at $3.20 per 1,000 gallons of metered blowdown. These are the rates in effect on 1 October 2025.
For planning purposes the Authority forecasts that both rates will increase by 3.5 percent per year in then-current dollars over the next thirty years. The forecast is the Authority's financial plan and includes general inflation.=====
PW-LTR-019 Amendment No. 1 to PW-LTR-014 - Data Annex Reclaimed Water Allocation
Papago Municipal Water and Wastewater Authority | 2 September 2026 | to the General Services Administration, Papago Federal Center
This letter amends the reclaimed water allocation confirmed in letter PW-LTR-014 of 3 July 2026 for the condenser water heat rejection replacement project.
1. Amended allocation
At the request of the General Services Administration, 700 thousand gallons per year of the firm annual allocation of the Data Annex Condenser Water Plant (ANNEX) are reassigned to the campus landscape irrigation meter with effect from 1 October 2026. The firm annual allocation of the ANNEX plant for evaporative heat rejection makeup is therefore 12,600 thousand gallons per year. The reassigned volume is not available to any heat rejection plant.
Plant served | Annual allocation, PW-LTR-014 (1,000 gal/yr) | Annual allocation as amended (1,000 gal/yr)
ANNEX - Data Annex Condenser Water Plant | 13,300 | 12,600

2. Unchanged terms
The peak day allocation and the blowdown discharge limit of the ANNEX plant, the allocations and limits of the CUP and LAB plants, the metering requirements and the rates of PW-LTR-014 are unchanged. All other terms of PW-LTR-014 remain in force.=====
UT-01 Electric Service - Rate Confirmation
Papago Electric Service Company | 22 September 2025 | to the General Services Administration, Papago Federal Center, Phoenix, Arizona
This letter confirms the rate schedule under which the Papago Federal Center campus takes electric service, for use in the life-cycle cost analysis of the condenser water heat rejection replacement. The campus is served at 12.47 kV through a single campus meter.
1. Applicable schedule
Rate Schedule GS-L, General Service - Large (commercial). The campus is a non-residential, non-industrial customer and is billed under the commercial general service schedules of the Company.
Charge | Rate in effect 1 October 2025 | Applies to
Energy charge | $0.0712 per kWh | All kWh, all hours, all months
Demand charge | $17.80 per kW per month | Billing demand
Basic service charge | $1,850.00 per month | Per meter; not affected by the load served

2. Billing demand
The billing demand for a month is the greater of (a) the highest 15-minute demand measured in that month and (b) 100 percent of the highest 15-minute demand measured in the preceding eleven months. Because of this ratchet, a load that adds to the campus peak adds to the billing demand of every month of the year.
3. Optional riders not elected
Time-of-use rider TOU-2 (on-peak energy $0.1184 per kWh from 3 pm to 8 pm on summer weekdays, off-peak $0.0561 per kWh) is available to this customer class but has NOT been elected for the campus, and the campus is not eligible to elect it before 2029. It does not apply to this analysis.
4. Price forecast
The Company does not publish a forecast of its rates for use in customer life-cycle cost analyses. Customers subject to federal life-cycle costing rules should apply the escalation those rules prescribe.

WT-01 Condenser Water Treatment Programme Memorandum
Papago Federal Center | Revision 1, 14 August 2026 | Prepared by Verde Basin Water Technologies, Inc. for the Engineer of Record
1. Supply
Condenser water makeup for all three plants is Class A+ reclaimed water delivered by the municipal purveyor from the reclamation facility, at the allocation and discharge limits of letter PW-LTR-014. The supply is the same for the three plants.
2. Analysis of record
The analysis of record for the supply is the most recent COMPLETE analysis in the Water Quality Portal result set in the project library, where a complete analysis is one that reports dissolved calcium, dissolved alkalinity, total dissolved solids in mg/L, dissolved sulfate and dissolved silica from the same sampling date. Field-parameter-only visits are not complete analyses. Earlier complete analyses in the same result set are superseded by the most recent one and must not be used for the selection.
Calcium is reported in the result set as mg/L as Ca. Calcium hardness as CaCO3 is the reported dissolved calcium multiplied by 2.497. The 'Hardness, Ca, Mg' result is total hardness and includes magnesium; it is not calcium hardness and must not be used in the indices. Where a determinand is reported both as dissolved and as recoverable, the dissolved result is used. Results reported in tons per acre-foot or tons per day are loading figures, not concentrations. Where total dissolved solids is reported in mg/L both as measured residue on evaporation and as a value computed from the constituents, the measured residue on evaporation is the value of record.
3. Programme
The programme is a phosphonate and polymer stabilised alkaline programme with sulphuric acid feed. The acid feed holds the circulating M-alkalinity at 120 ppm as CaCO3 at all cycles of concentration; alkalinity therefore does not cycle up. Total dissolved solids and calcium hardness cycle up in proportion to the cycles of concentration. A conductivity controller with an automatic blowdown valve and metering pumps for the inhibitor and the biocide are required at every plant, as is a makeup water meter.
4. Controlling cycles of concentration
The allowable cycles of concentration are the lowest of the limits the adopted water treatment manual gives for the scale-forming salts that this programme does not address, and the limit that the calcium carbonate scaling index of the same manual permits. The inhibitor package addresses calcium carbonate AND calcium sulfate, so neither the manual's rough calcium carbonate prediction nor its calcium sulfate prediction is a controlling limit here; calcium phosphate is not applicable because the circulating orthophosphate is held below 10 ppm by the programme. Silica is not addressed by the programme and its limit applies as the manual states it.
The programme is qualified by the supplier to a computed Practical (Puckorius) Scaling Index of not less than 5.60. Below that value the dispersant cannot hold calcium carbonate in solution and the programme is not warranted. The index is evaluated at the hottest waterside temperature of the system, which for these plants is the condenser water return temperature at the design point - the return temperature the selected cells actually produce there (the CWR the calculation workbook's design point sheet reports), not a scheduled figure - and at the circulating concentrations that the selected cycles of concentration produce.
4.1 Evaluation of the index factors
Factor B is taken from the manual's temperature table by linear interpolation. Factors A, C and D are the closed forms that the manual's tables tabulate, adopted here so that the index can be evaluated where the circulating concentration leaves the tabulated range:
    A = (log10(total dissolved solids in ppm) - 1) / 10
    C = log10(calcium hardness as CaCO3 in ppm) - 0.4
    D = log10(M-alkalinity as CaCO3 in ppm)
These reproduce the manual's tables across their whole tabulated range. The equilibrium pH is the closed form the manual's appendix gives as an alternative to its chart.
5. Other limits
Circulating pH is controlled to 8.0 to 8.6. The blowdown discharged to the sanitary sewer must not exceed the daily limit of PW-LTR-014. Legionella control follows the campus water management plan and does not change the water balance.
6. Programme cost
The programme is supplied as a full-service contract: inhibitor, dispersant, biocide, sulphuric acid, controller service and monthly testing, billed at $0.42 per 1,000 gallons of makeup water treated, at prices in effect on 1 October 2025. The contract price is adjusted for general inflation only.

RFI-031 Response - Weather Basis, Redundancy Basis and Condenser Water Setpoint Policy
Papago Federal Center | Response issued 21 August 2026 | Engineer of Record: Sandoval Klee Mechanical Engineers, PC
Question 1
The adopted HVAC criteria and the adopted agency facilities standard give different outdoor wet-bulb bases for evaporative machines. Which governs the tower selection, and which governs the failure-case calculation?
Response 1
Both govern, for different calculations, and neither is waived. Size the cells - the design point, the scheduled design approach and the redundancy capacity check - on the basis the HVAC criteria give for open cooling towers and wet closed-circuit cooling towers, which is the 1.0 percent annual wet-bulb temperature with the adder that clause states. Perform the cooling robustness (largest machine out of service) calculation on the evaporation design wet-bulb basis the agency facilities standard names in its cooling robustness requirement, with the same adder applied. Compute both percentiles from the station period of record identified in DC-02 paragraph 5.1. The cancelled engineering weather data criteria document in the project library is not a source of design values on this project.
Question 2
The agency standard requires variable frequency drives on the tower fans to control the condenser water supply temperature to the chillers, but does not state a reset policy. What policy should be scheduled?
Response 2
Schedule a wet-bulb-following reset with two numbers: a supply temperature floor and an offset above the outdoor wet-bulb temperature. The setpoint at any hour is the larger of the two, limited below by the minimum entering condenser water temperature of the chillers served. Both numbers are the designer's to optimise and both must appear on the tower schedule. A fixed setpoint is a special case with a zero offset and is not prohibited, but it is unlikely to be the least-energy policy at this site.
Question 3
The project library contains two industrial water treatment criteria documents with the same clause numbering, and two revisions of the roof mechanical plan. Which govern?
Response 3
The 2026 manual governs the water treatment criteria; the 2023 criteria document it replaced is retained for reference only. Revision C of M-401 governs the roof; Revision B is superseded and its equipment zone and outdoor air intake locations must not be used. Both supersessions are recorded in DC-02 paragraph 2.=====
RFI-034 Response - Retained Loads on the Motor Control Centers
Papago Federal Center | Response issued 4 September 2026 | Engineer of Record: Sandoval Klee Mechanical Engineers, PC
Question 1
The Laboratory Wing exhaust fan replacement, a separate contract, connects new exhaust fan motors to MCC-R3 before the heat rejection plant is commissioned. Panel schedule E-601 Revision C was prepared from the field survey of 19 February 2026. Does the spare capacity E-601 states for MCC-R3 account for these motors?
Response 1
No. The three laboratory exhaust fans EF-L7, EF-L8 and EF-L9 were not connected at the time of the survey and are not in the retained existing demand of E-601. Each fan is driven by a 7.5 hp, 4 pole, totally enclosed fan cooled motor with a nominal full-load efficiency of 91.7 percent, through a variable frequency drive with an efficiency of 0.97 at rated load. The fans serve fume hood exhaust and run continuously at full speed and full nameplate load, so they operate coincident with the heat rejection plant at every hour of the year. Add their electrical input to the retained existing demand of MCC-R3 and reduce the spare capacity available to the new heat rejection plant accordingly. The bus rating and the continuous loading limit stated on E-601 are unchanged.
Question 2
Are MCC-R1 and MCC-R2 affected?
Response 2
No. No load has been connected to MCC-R1 or MCC-R2 since the survey, and their spare capacities are as E-601 states.

import m, math, json
from search2 import simulate, lcc_of, basic
CANDS={
 'CUP':[('CTX-0600-S',4,[1800],[60,65,70,75],[10,11,12,13,14])],
 'ANNEX':[('CTX-0600-S',4,[1800],[75,78,80,82,85,88],[8,9,10,11,12]),

 'LAB':[('CTX-0900-H',3,[2025],[55,60,65,70],[7,8,9,10])],
}
if __name__=='__main__':
    BAS={pl:basic(pl) for pl in ('CUP','ANNEX','LAB')}
    out=[]
    for pl in ('CUP','ANNEX','LAB'):
        p=m.PLANTS[pl]
        for mod,nc,flows,floors,offs in CANDS[pl]:
            for flow in flows:
                for floor in floors:
                    for off in offs:
                        cfg=dict(model=mod,cells=nc,gpm=float(flow),cwsmin=float(floor),cwsoffset=float(off))
                        res,d=simulate(pl,cfg)
                        el=lcc_of(pl,cfg,res)
                        rec=dict(pl=pl,cfg=cfg,pk=res['pk'],Et=res['Et'],mk=res['mk'],bd=res['bd'],ev=res['ev'],
                                 redcap=res['redcap'],coc=res['coc'],maxcoc=res['maxcoc'],psi=res['psi'],
                                 cws=res['dp']['cws_act'],cwr=res['dp']['cwr'],app=res['dp']['ta_full'],rng=res['dp']['Tr'],
                                 inv=el['inv'],lcc=el['lcc'],NS=BAS[pl]['lcc']-el['lcc'],fails=res['fails'],
                                 pdmk=res['pdmk'],pdbd=res['pdbd'],Ec=res['Ec'],Ef=res['Ef'],Ep=res['Ep'])
                        out.append(rec)
                        print('%-5s %-12s n%d f%5d fl%2d o%2d | pk %6.1f/%4.0f mk %6.0f/%5.0f pd %5.0f red %5.0f COC %.2f cws %.1f app %.2f | NS %7.0f | %s'%(

    json.dump(dict(basic=BAS,rows=out),open('search3.json','w'),indent=1)
EOF

SECTION 23 65 00 - COOLING TOWERS
Papago Federal Center, Condenser Water Heat Rejection Replacement | Issued for construction documents, 14 August 2026
PART 1 - GENERAL
1.1 Summary
Factory assembled, induced draught, counterflow, film fill, field erected on structural steel dunnage, open evaporative cooling tower cells with variable frequency driven fans, for condenser water service.
1.2 Performance certification
Thermal performance of each cell must be certified under CTI Standard STD-201 for the scheduled duty. Where a model is not certified, a field acceptance test under CTI ATC-105 at the contractor's expense is required.
PART 2 - PRODUCTS
2.1 Acceptable manufacturers
Cells of the CTX Series C range in submittal VD-01, or an approved equal of the same certified capability, plan dimensions and operating weight.
2.2 Materials
Water contact surfaces, including the cold water basin, the casing below the operating water line, the distribution basin and all fasteners in the water stream, must comply with the materials requirement of the agency facilities standard for cooling towers. Confirm the selected material option against that requirement; the manufacturer offers options that do not comply. Structural steel dunnage is hot-dip galvanised after fabrication; dunnage is not a water contact surface.
2.3 Drift eliminators
Cellular PVC drift eliminators, removable in sections. The certified drift rate of the selected eliminator must not exceed 0.002 percent of the design circulating water flow rate at design air flow. Eliminator classes and their certified drift rates are in submittal VD-04. The drift rate used in the water balance must be the certified rate of the eliminator actually selected.
2.4 Basin and blowdown
Cold water basin with a sloped sump, sweeper piping, an overflow, a drain, a make-up connection with an electrically actuated valve and an air gap, and an electrically actuated automatic blowdown valve controlled from a conductivity controller. Provide connections and mounting for the chemical metering pumps of the water treatment programme. A basin heater and heat traced make-up piping are provided only where the design criteria memorandum requires them.
2.5 Fans and drives
Axial propeller fans on right angle gear reducers, with a variable frequency drive on each fan motor. Fan motors are totally enclosed fan cooled, squirrel cage induction, NEMA Design B, suitable for inverter duty, and must comply with the federal energy conservation standard for the applicable motor category. The fan must not draw more than the motor nameplate horsepower at any operating point in the scheduled sequence; the gear reducer service factor is not available as fan power.
2.6 Sound
The A-weighted sound power level of each cell at full fan speed must not exceed 102 dB re 1 pW. Sound power levels of the offered cells are in submittal VD-01.
2.7 Equalising and isolation
Where more than one cell is installed, provide equalising lines between the cold water basins and automatic isolation valves on the supply to each cell, so that any cell may be taken out of service with its chiller running, as the agency facilities standard requires.
PART 3 - EXECUTION
3.1 Installation
Set cells on structural steel dunnage on the roof framing zones indicated on S-401, within the equipment zone indicated on M-401 Revision C. Maintain the air inlet clearances of submittal VD-01 on every air inlet face and between adjacent cells, and the clearance between the top of the roof and the underside of the basin that the agency facilities standard requires.

2.1 Closed loop chilled water and heating hot water
Provide a nitrite-molybdate closed system inhibitor at 800 to 1,200 ppm as nitrite, with a tolyltriazole yellow metal inhibitor at 5 to 10 ppm. Maintain closed system pH between 8.5 and 10.5. Closed systems do not concentrate and have no cycles of concentration, no blowdown and no evaporative makeup.
2.2 Glycol
Where freeze protection is required, use inhibited propylene glycol at 30 percent by volume, with a freeze point of -13 deg F and a burst point of -60 deg F. Ethylene glycol is prohibited. Correct the pump head and the heat transfer capacity for the glycol properties at the operating temperature: at 30 percent propylene glycol the specific heat is 0.90 and the specific gravity is 1.02 at 100 deg F, so the flow required for a given duty and range increases by approximately 9 percent.

Provide a 55 gallon glycol feed unit with a pressure switch, a low level alarm and a backflow preventer for each closed system requiring glycol.

hierarchy below. The documents applied are:

5-2 
COOLING TOWER WATER CALCULATIONS 
5-2.1 
Principles of Cooling Tower System Operations. 
The function of a cooling tower is to dissipate heat from water-cooled refrigeration, air-
conditioning and industrial process systems. Water is typically the heat transfer medium 
used to dissipate the heat. A cooling tower uses a combination of heat and mass 
transfer (evaporation) to cool the water flowing through the tower. Conductive heat 
transfer accounts for 20 to 30 percent of the total heat dissipated. The remaining 70 to 
80 percent of total cooling is the result of evaporative cooling of about 1 to 2 percent of 
the recirculating water, depending on the decrease in temperature across the tower. It 
takes approximately 2,326,000 joules to evaporate 1000 BTU per 1 pound of water (1 
kilogram of water). If this amount of heat is extracted from 1000 pounds (454 kilograms) 
of water, approximately 1 pound (0.45 kilogram) of water will be evaporated and the 
temperature will drop 1° F (0.55° C). If 10 pounds (4.5 kilograms) of water are 
evaporated, the water temperature will drop 10° F (5.5° C). The water lost by evaporation 
is replaced with makeup water. Water is also added to replace water lost through tower 
drift (loss of water from the tower as a fine mist), leaks in the system (unintentional 
blowdown), and water discharged as intentional blowdown. Water that is added to the 
cooling tower to replace all of these losses is known as cooling tower makeup water.

5-2.1.1 
Relationship between Evaporation, Blowdown, and Makeup. 
The operation of cooling towers can be described by the relationship between 
evaporation, blowdown, and makeup. Makeup water must equal blowdown water plus 
water evaporation to maintain a constant operating water level in the system: 
Equation 5-1. 
Operation of Cooling Towers 
𝑀𝑀= 𝐵𝐵+ 𝐸𝐸 
Where: 
M = makeup water, gpm (liters/sec) 
B = blowdown, gpm (liters/sec) (all sources) 
E = evaporation, gpm (liters/sec) 
NOTE: Blowdown (B) includes discharge to sewer, drift loss, and any leaks from the 
system. 
EXAMPLE:  
M = 100 gpm (6.3 liters/sec) 
B = 10 gpm (0.63 liters/sec) 
E = 90 gpm (5.67 liters/sec) 
5-2.1.2 
Cycles of Concentration (COC). 
One of the common terms used in describing the water use efficiency of cooling tower 
water systems is COC. COC represents the relationship between the makeup water 
quantity and blowdown quantity. COC is a measure of the total amount of minerals that 
is concentrated in the cooling tower water relative to the amount of minerals in the 
makeup water or to the volume of each type of water. The higher the COC, the greater 
the water use efficiency. Most cooling tower systems operate with a COC of 3 to 10, 
where 3 represents acceptable efficiency and 10 represents very good efficiency. It has 
been found that the range of 5 to 7 COC represents the most cost-effective situation.

Controlling COC. 
A simple, sometimes overlooked rule: To increase COC, decrease blowdown; to 
decrease COC, increase blowdown. 
5-2.1.2.4 
Relationship between COC and Makeup. 
COC and makeup requirements are related to the temperature drop across a cooling 
tower and to the recirculating rate of the tower. As shown in Figure 5-15, for a 
recirculating tower with water temperature drops of 10° F (5.5° C), 20° F (11° C), and 
30° F (16.5° C), the makeup water requirement decreases rapidly as COC is increased 
to about 4 or 5, with lower incremental reductions at higher COC; therefore, COC can 
be adjusted (increased) to allow for reductions in water use (water conservation) and for 
reductions in the amount of water treatment chemicals used.

## 9. Life-cycle cost analysis

The base date is 1 October 2025, with a one-year design and construction period and beneficial occupancy on
1 October 2026 (EC-01 2 and 3). The study period is 26 years from the base date: one construction year plus
the 25-year service life of the longest-lived admissible casing (SS-304 or SS-316), as 10 CFR
436.14(d)(2)(i) requires for mutually exclusive alternatives. Investment is a lump sum at the base date;
energy, water and non-fuel O&M costs accrue from beneficial occupancy, so their present values use the
2025 supplement's factors for years 2 through 26, that is the tabulated 26-year factor less its year-1
term (10 CFR 436.16(c), 436.17(b), 436.17(d)).

The real discount rate is 3.0 percent (the DOE floor in the 2025 Discount Rate Memo). The electricity
uniform present worth factor is that of the 2025 supplement for Arizona, Mountain division, commercial

beneficial occupancy in year 2, so the factor used is 16.30610 - 0.97087 = 15.33522. The water factor
restates the Authority's 3.5 percent nominal forecast with the supplement's 1.5 percent long-term inflation
rate, giving a 1.9704 percent real escalation, and uses years 2-26: 21.77700. The non-fuel O&M factor is the

## 4. Evaporation formulation

The water balance, the allocation and discharge checks and the `WaterBalance` sheet use the
**SATURATED-EXIT** formulation of DC-02 paragraph 7, the moist-air method of the adopted reference
implementation's tower water-use routine: the inlet air enthalpy is that of saturated air at the inlet
wet-bulb temperature, the outlet air is saturated at the inlet enthalpy plus the water-side heat rejection
divided by the air mass flow, and the evaporated mass is the air mass flow times the rise in specific
humidity, converted to a volume with the density of water. The water density is the DC-02 7 expression
rho = 1000 x (1 - (T + 288.9414)/(508929.2 x (T + 68.12963)) x (T - 3.9863)^2) kg/m3 at the mean of the
inlet dry-bulb and the saturated outlet air temperatures, not below 4 deg C. Blowdown is E/(COC-1) less
drift and makeup is the sum of evaporation, drift and blowdown. Drift is the certified DE-2 rate applied to
the design flow per cell, the number of cells in service and the air flow ratio (VD-04 1).

SATURATED-EXIT is also the formulation EC-01 paragraph 6 requires the life-cycle cost analysis to price,
so the water balance and the life-cycle cost use the same water quantities. The LOSS-FACTOR formulation of
UFM 3-230-13 is not used anywhere in the package; it is recorded here only to state the choice. Each
workbook declares `EvaporationMethod = saturated-exit`, and the schedule declares
`EVAPMETHOD = SATURATED-EXIT`; the two agree.

## 5. Calculation method

* **Tower.** Each cell is modelled with the variable-speed `CoolingTowerPerformance:YorkCalc` correlation
  (counterflow) of the adopted performance data set: the approach is evaluated at the water flow rate
  ratio, air flow rate ratio, inlet wet bulb and range, in the SI units of the object, and converted to
  deg F. The object's limits are applied at every scenario (WFR 0.75-1.25, range 2-40 deg F, approach
  2-72 deg F, L/G <= 8); the inlet wet bulb is clamped to the object's 26.6667 deg C maximum, which is the
  design value at this site, and the water flow rate ratio is never clamped or extrapolated (DC-02 6.8).
* **Fan.** Full speed when the full-speed outlet is warmer than the setpoint; modulation between the 30
  percent minimum controllable air flow and full speed to hold the setpoint; minimum-speed cycling below
  that; free convection at an air flow ratio of 0.125 with the fan off. Fan shaft power follows the cube
  law of VD-02, divided by the motor efficiency and the 0.97 VFD efficiency to give electrical input.
* **Chiller.** The three procured machines are modelled with their `Chiller:Electric:EIR` data sets:
  available capacity = reference capacity x CAPFT at the design leaving chilled water temperature and the
  operating entering condenser water temperature; power = (available capacity/COP_ref) x EIRFT x
  EIRFPLR(PLR) x cycling fraction. The entering condenser water temperature is the tower supply
  temperature. Staging is the smallest number of machines whose available capacity (CAPFT x reference
  capacity, without the maximum part-load ratio) meets the block load (DC-02 6.5).
* **Pumps.** One constant-speed pump per running chiller, head H = H_static + (H_pipe + H_condenser)
  (Q/Q_ref)^2 with the DC-02 6.4 constants, shaft power QH/(3960 eta) and electrical input
  shaft x 0.7457/eta_motor.
* **Cells.** Cells are isolated one at a time only when the per-cell flow would fall below the effective
  minimum, the larger of the VD-01 minimum flow and 0.75 x nominal (DC-02 6.6). Fans of cells in service
  modulate together.
* **Reset.** CWS setpoint = larger of the scheduled floor and outdoor wet bulb + offset, never below the
  chiller minimum entering condenser water temperature (DC-02 6.7). A condenser water bypass holds the
  setpoint when the tower would otherwise overcool. Floors and offsets: CUP 65 deg F / 11 deg F; ANNEX
  80 deg F / 11.5 deg F; LAB 58 deg F / 8.5 deg F.
* **Design point.** All chillers and all cells in service at full fan speed at 80.0 deg F wet bulb and the
  design block load. `DesignPoint` reports the achieved values; the DXF carries the scheduled, conservative
  CWS, which is the reset setpoint at the design wet bulb (91.0 / 90.0 / 88.0 deg F).
* **Redundancy.** Largest cell out of service, design condenser water flow unchanged, remaining cells at
  full fan speed, at 81.0 deg F wet bulb (evaluated at the object's 80.0 deg F clamp). Redundancy capacity
  is the sum of the machines' available capacity at the CWS the remaining cells produce.

# Design basis - Condenser water heat rejection replacement, Papago Federal Center, Phoenix, Arizona

Revision C issue, September 2026 (incorporating RFI-031 of 21 August 2026 and RFI-034 of 4 September
2026). Prepared for the General Services Administration by Sandoval Klee Mechanical Engineers, PC. This
basis accompanies `CT_SCHEDULE_CUP.dxf`, `CT_CALC_CUP.xlsx`, `CT_SCHEDULE_ANNEX.dxf`,
`CT_CALC_ANNEX.xlsx`, `CT_SCHEDULE_LAB.dxf` and `CT_CALC_LAB.xlsx`.

## 1. Governing documents and status

DC-02 Revision 3 (14 August 2026) is the governing design-criteria memorandum and is the authority for the
hierarchy below. The documents applied are:

* UFC 3-410-01, *Heating, Ventilating and Air Conditioning Systems* (28 July 2025, Change 1) - adopted in
  full; governs the outdoor design condition for equipment sizing (paragraph 2-4.2.4).
* GSA PBS-P100, *Facilities Standards for the Public Buildings Service* (2024) - adopted in full; governs
  plant configuration, the cooling-robustness (redundancy) wet-bulb basis (5.1.3), siting separations
  (Table 5.2), materials (5.3.3.11) and the roof-to-basin clearance (5.3.2.3).
* UFM 3-230-13, *Industrial Water Treatment* (5 February 2026) - adopted for the treatment programme, the
  water balance and the scaling indices.
* UFC 3-230-13 (2023) - SUPERSEDED by UFM 3-230-13; retained for reference only and not cited as
  authority. UFC 3-400-02 (2018, Change 2) - CANCELLED; retained for reference only and not cited as
  authority; no design value is taken from it.
* 10 CFR Part 431 Subpart B (electric motors) and 10 CFR Part 436 Subpart A (life-cycle cost).
* EC-01 Life-Cycle Cost Analysis Criteria, Revision 0 - adopted; the base date, schedule, basic design,
  cost data and study period of the life-cycle cost analysis.
* *Annual Supplement to NIST Handbook 135*, 2025 edition (NIST data release doi:10.18434/mds2-3848) -
  adopted as the source of the discount rate and present-value factors. NIST IR 85-3273-39 (2024 edition)
  is SUPERSEDED and none of its rates, factors or example numbers is used.
* EnergyPlus reference implementation source (`CondenserLoopTowers.cc`, `ChillerElectricEIR.cc`,
  `Psychrometrics.cc`/`.hh`, `CurveManager.cc`) and the performance data sets `Chillers.idf` and
  `PerfCurves.idf` - adopted as the simulation basis: the variable-speed tower approach correlation and its
  validity limits, the fan power and water-use treatment, the electric chiller capacity and input-ratio
  model, and the psychrometric property relations.
* Section 23 65 00 - Cooling Towers (14 August 2026). Section 23 25 00 is a closed-hydronic excerpt and
  does not apply to the open condenser water system.
* WT-01 Revision 1 (14 August 2026); PW-LTR-014 (3 July 2026); PW-LTR-019 Amendment No. 1 (2 September
  2026); UT-01 (22 September 2025); RFI-031 (21 August 2026); RFI-034 (4 September 2026).
* M-401 Revision C (31 July 2026) - governs the equipment zones and outdoor air intake positions. M-401
  Revision B is SUPERSEDED and its zones and intakes are not used. S-401 Revision C (31 July 2026) governs
  the allowable superimposed loads. E-501 and E-601 Revision C govern the motor control centres.
* Vendor submittals VD-01 to VD-05 (reviewed, 2026).

## 2. Documented conflicts

CONFLICT 1: ADOPTED UFC 3-410-01 2-4.2.4 | SET ASIDE GSA PBS-P100 5.3.1

CONFLICT 2: ADOPTED UFM 3-230-13 5-3 | SET ASIDE UFC 3-230-13 5-3

CONFLICT 3: ADOPTED M-401 Revision C | SET ASIDE M-401 Revision B

Conflict 1 is resolved as DC-02 paragraph 2 allocates outdoor design conditions for equipment sizing to the
adopted HVAC criteria: the tower is sized on the 1.0 percent annual wet bulb plus the 5 deg F adder of UFC
3-410-01 paragraph 2-4.2.4, not on the 0.4 percent dew-point basis named in PBS-P100 paragraph 5.3.1. The
0.4 percent evaporation design wet bulb that PBS-P100 5.1.3 names is retained for the cooling-robustness
(redundancy) calculation only, with the same 5 deg F adder (DC-02 5.2, 6.3 and RFI-031 Response 1); the two
bases are therefore applied to the two different calculations the two documents govern, and neither is
waived. Conflict 2 is the edition conflict between the two industrial water treatment manuals; DC-02
paragraph 2 and RFI-031 Response 3 make the 2026 UFM the governing edition, and the 2023 document is not
cited as authority. Conflict 3 is the roof plan revision; DC-02 paragraph 2 and RFI-031 Response 3 make
M-401 Revision C governing, and Revision B's zones and intake positions are not used.

Two further disagreements in the library are resolved by the same hierarchy. PBS-P100 paragraph 5.3.3.11
prohibits galvanised steel on water-contact surfaces while the VD-01 standard offering is the G-235
galvanised casing; the project requirement governs and SS-304 is selected. PBS-P100 paragraph 5.3.5.3 caps
open-system total dissolved solids at 1,500 ppm while the reclaimed supply already contains 1,720 ppm before
any concentration; DC-02 paragraph 2 expressly states that the cap does not govern this reclaimed-water
supply and that the alkalinity range of the same paragraph is met by the WT-01 acid feed, so no
cycles-of-concentration limit is taken from PBS-P100. The 2024 NIST supplement is superseded by the 2025
data release for every rate and factor (EC-01 4), and Section 23 25 00 is expressly a closed-hydronic
excerpt that does not apply to the open condenser water system.

## 3. Weather basis

Governing station: Phoenix Airport (NCEI station 72278023183), Local Climatological Data for the three
complete calendar years 2022, 2023 and 2024 (DC-02 5.1). Only FM-15 and FM-16 observations are used; daily
and monthly summary rows are excluded. The resulting period of record is 26,527 hourly observations.

Percentiles are taken over the whole POR as one annual population (DC-02 5.2):

* 1.0 percent annual wet bulb = 75.0 deg F; design outdoor wet bulb for tower sizing = 75.0 + 5.0 =
  **80.0 deg F** (UFC 3-410-01 2-4.2.4).
* 0.4 percent annual wet bulb = 76.0 deg F; failure-case (redundancy) wet bulb = 76.0 + 5.0 =
  **81.0 deg F** (PBS-P100 5.1.3, DC-02 5.2 and 6.3, RFI-031 Response 1).
* 99.6 percent annual dry bulb = **41.0 deg F** (DC-02 5.4). It is above 32 deg F, so no basin heater and
  no heat-traced makeup are required; `BASINHEATER` is NO on all three schedules.

The two adopted documents state the wet-bulb basis differently and the difference is applied deliberately:
UFC 3-410-01 2-4.2.4 (1.0 percent + 5 deg F) governs tower selection and the design point, while PBS-P100
5.1.3 (0.4 percent evaporation design wet bulb + 5 deg F) governs the failure case only. The design wet
bulb of 80.0 deg F coincides with the maximum inlet wet bulb of the adopted YorkCalc performance object
(26.6667 deg C); the reference implementation clamps the inlet wet bulb there and the value is not
extrapolated (DC-02 6.8, RFI-031 Response 1).

Mean station pressure over the POR = 28.722 inHg = 97,264 Pa; this is the barometric pressure used in the
psychrometric routines (DC-02 5.5). The scenario bins are 2 deg F wet-bulb bins and 5 deg F dry-bulb bins
with edges at whole multiples of the width from zero, bin mid-points, and counts scaled to 8760 hours per
year (DC-02 5.3). The 180 populated bins sum to exactly 8760 hours. Where a dry-bulb mid-point falls below
its wet-bulb mid-point the dry bulb is set equal to the wet-bulb mid-point.

All deliverables are present, complete, and validated. Final verification results:

## Files at the exact path
`/filesystem/final_batch4__mechanical_task3_ct_heat_lcc__blind/output/submission.zip` (134,099 bytes, 8 files, `unzip -t` OK):

```

CT_SCHEDULE_ANNEX.dxf   CT_CALC_ANNEX.xlsx
CT_SCHEDULE_LAB.dxf     CT_CALC_LAB.xlsx
constraint_register.csv design_basis.md
```

## Validation
- `ahpele_check.py` on the zip → **no problems found** (all formats parse).
- Schema enumeration script → **NONE**: every DXF cell key (11) and plant key (14), one closed polyline per installed cell, `G-TBLK` revision, five exact workbook sheets, every required `DesignPoint`/`WaterBalance`/`Energy`/`LifeCycleCost` key numeric, `OffDesign` 17 columns × 180 rows all numeric with Hours = 8,760, evaporation method agrees, register 95 × 6 CSV rows, design basis with 3 governing lines and 3 conflict lines.
- `ahpele_reqscan.py --check` → **82/82 strong candidates reviewed, 0 unreviewed**.
- My engineering audit (rebuilds each plant from its DXF, recomputes energy/water/LCC, checks all hard limits, geometry, clearances, structural loads, COC/PSI, allocations, MCC, redundancy, validity envelope, L/G, totals) → **0 failures**.

## Final design
| Plant | Cells / model | Flow (gpm) | Floor/offset (°F) | COC | CWS sched / achieved (°F) | Peak / MCC (kW) | Makeup / allocation (kgal) | NS (USD) | Governing constraint |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| CUP | 4 × CTX-0600-S | 1,800 | 65 / 11 | 4.13 | 91.0 / 85.36 | 513.0 / 528 | 9,743 / 10,300 | 240,555 | structural capacity 0.0250 |
| ANNEX | 4 × CTX-0600-S | 1,800 | 80 / 11.5 | 3.99 | 91.5 / 85.69 | 570.7 / 590 | 12,555 / 12,600 | 246,666 | water allocation 0.0035 |
| LAB | 3 × CTX-0900-H | 2,025 | 58 / 8.5 | 3.86 | 88.5 / 85.99 | 633.1 / 641.14 | 17,057 / 17,400 | 290,978 | electrical capacity 0.0125 |

Design wet bulb 80.0 °F (1.0 % 75.0 + 5), redundancy wet bulb 81.0 °F (0.4 % 76.0 + 5), 99.6 % dry bulb 41.0 °F (no basin heater), SATURATED-EXIT water balance, SS-304 casings/basins, DE-2 eliminators, premium-efficiency 6-pole TEFC motors, 4 ft basin clearance. All redundancy capacities exceed the block loads; all condenser/cell flow, WFR and L/G limits are met; all three plants are inside the reclaimed-water allocation, peak-day and blowdown limits and the MCC spare capacities.

The independent findings and their dispositions (including the one part of finding 5 rejected — the peak-day test is the PW-LTR-014 design day, not the highest-rate bin) are appended to `/tmp/ahpele/independent_review.md`.
